thesis_break_reason: Below ~$85 (EV ~ $1.3T) the market would be pricing the bear state - a compute glut or a capacity/funding stall - rather than our base of 8.5 GW with prices holding through 2027; that level is ~20% under the post-IPO low ($104.83) and close to the SOTP run-off value with a fast fade, so it would mean the spot price per watt has started to break (renewals below $35/W-yr) or the build has stalled, not ordinary volatility.

key_uncertainties: Durability of the compute shortage: hold through 2027 then fade (base) vs hold into 2029 (bull) vs glut in 2028 (bear) - the single largest value driver (fleet part $168B to $1.1T).
YE2027 capacity: 8.5 GW base vs 13 GW claimed; funding (~$270B SI capex) and GPU/power supply are the binding constraints.
Older-chip price decay per watt: on-demand indices imply ~0.6 at age 3, one-year contract indices ~0.3.
Whether the market keeps paying mega-cap multiples for peak-scarcity EBITDA (our 11x/20x vs Kilian 15x/27x moves fair value by ~29%).
Lock-up supply: ~1.6B shares in the next week, Musk's 6.4B in June 2027.
Tesla combination terms and governance; Starship Flight 15 and full reuse timing; customer concentration (Anthropic $1.25B/month, 90-day notice).

reverse_dcf_check: 11x NTM EBITDA (~$200B) implies the compute EBITDA holds roughly flat after 2028 with capex at maintenance, i.e. new-chip prices near ~$45/W-yr into the 2030s - about twice the 21.5 $/W-yr NPV-0 price; our run-off says it halves by 2030, which is why the SOTP leg is ~60% below the multiple legs. Today's EV (~$2.14T incl. EchoStar) needs ~$51/W-yr held forever on our 8.5 GW path.

The Cursor acquisition-related SBC ($23.4B over vesting, $1,217M in Q3) is excluded from EBIT because the 389.3M merger shares are already outstanding and the assumed RSUs/options are in the dilutive count - counted once. reasoning: Q3-26 (Ex. 99.1): revenue $14.6B (+161%), SI $7.6B, 1.7 GW nameplate (+0.3 GW q/q), capex $19.6B; call: Q4 capex $35-40B (~2x the August guide), Q1-27 revenue $33-37B, CFO 'slightly above the high end of $30-50 per watt', Musk '13 GW total' at YE27. We score management: compute near-term targets get raised (YE26 >2 GW to 2.5-3) but long-dated operating targets slip badly (V3 satellites, Starship cadence), giving a record-adjusted 8.9 GW; funding (~$270B of 2027 SI capex) and GPU supply give ~8.5 GW, our base. Shortage durability: prices rose through 2026 (Uvik; SemiAnalysis H100 index), 2027 hyperscaler capex ~$1.3T is still power-limited, so we hold ~$48/W-yr through 2027 and fade from 2028 to the 21.5 $/W-yr NPV-0 price by ~2031, as the 2023-25 H100 cycle did within ~2 years. The fleet run-off at spot (Kilian's method) is worth ~$509B at the horizon, Starlink $258B, SOTP $57/share after 10% holdco, net debt ~$58B and EchoStar; the multiple legs on peak-scarcity NTM EBITDA give $148 (11x) and $130 (20x). Blend $108. Ladder: mixture of bear $58 (25%), base $120 (50%), bull $235 (25%) with 22-28% within-state vol; median ~$118, P(>= spot) ~0.31 - shrunk toward the market because the fade timing is the least certain input. The market ($2.14T EV) needs ~$51/W-yr forever; we think it fades, but momentum, Musk optionality (orbital compute, Tesla) and a tight float keep a fat right tail. Research was primary-filing led (424B4 lock-up table, CORRESP, Cursor 8-K, Tesla 10-Q); transcript numbers are quotes, labelled estimates; no option data used.

model_inputs.structure_note: Value carried by Kilian's standing legs: 0.4 consolidated EV/EBITDA (11x NTM GAAP EBITDA) + 0.4 sum of the parts + 0.2 P/E (20x NTM). The SOTP is the deep model: SI compute fleet as a run-off by vintage at spot (2024-28 vintages, every watt incl. Grok's at spot, no terminal value, $8/W salvage), a 2029-30 build window at 6 GW/yr (new-chip price stays above the 21.5 $/W-yr NPV-0 price until ~2031, so later capacity earns its cost of capital), Starlink subscriber DCF to 2035 then NOPAT/WACC (RONIC = WACC), Space as Starship success/delay/failure (with the Starlink knock-on), Cursor at its $60B mark, X at $12B, Grok at NPV 0, 10% holdco discount, all cash-flow parts at 9.19%. Consolidated years FY2026-28 come from the same build (segment_build: Space, Connectivity, SI). Net debt at the horizon is stated directly (net_debt_horizon) because Q4-26 capex is ~45% of FY2026 capex and the engine's pro-rata bridge would understate the burn.
model_inputs.gap_note: 1) Multiples: we use 11x EV/EBITDA and 20x P/E instead of Kilian's 15x / 27x; with his multiples the set values at $139.67 vs $108.28 (+29%), so this goes to Kilian. Reason: NTM EBITDA at the horizon is ~85% compute rented at ~2.2x the NPV-0 price on 90-day-cancellable terms (424B4/10-Q); our own price path halves it by 2030, so a mega-cap multiple on it double-counts durability the SOTP says is not there. 2) The SOTP ($57/share) and the multiple legs ($148/$130) disagree by >50%: the multiples capitalise peak-scarcity EBITDA, the run-off charges the fade and the ~$290B/yr capex. 3) Judgment calls for Kilian: YE27 capacity 8.5 GW (vs 13 claimed); price hold through 2027 then fade to ~$21/W-yr by 2032; Space option $50B in the success state only; external rental share 65%/55% in the consolidated legs.
